October 22 test-build retest

Updated Oct 22, 2026, 3:48 PM Eastern. Windows 0.1.100 and Android 1.51-tester35 (build 85) are installed test builds, not public downloads. At that time the public downloads were Windows 0.1.99 and Android tester34; Windows 0.1.102 was published later (Oct 24, 2026, 1:05 PM Eastern) and tester35 was not. The coordinator reports viewer/server repairs deployed October 22 at 6:49 AM Eastern and the older-TV-browser navigation repair at 7:24 AM Eastern. RETEST-1 reports 14 of 18 items passed; the other four include a child delete-screen failure, sidecar subtitles selected but not drawn, inconsistent online Next and network-dependent offline wording. Folder poster/NFO handling has no recorded repair. No new feature tick is justified.

The browser repair has split delivery: the server portion is reported deployed at 6:49 AM Eastern on October 22, with a further TV-browser server repair at 7:24 AM; the desktop-player portion is in unpublished Windows 0.1.100. The affected PC and combined away-route repair still need retesting.

Owner-reported on October 22: on a friend’s Samsung TV built-in browser, playback away from home and Skip intro worked after repeated Reconnect clicks; ordinary poster/sidebar navigation failed without that extra step, and Up next/Next were absent at the credits. The fixed-build retry, exact TV model, browser version and served build are unconfirmed. Earlier Chromecast viewing is a separate observation with sender details unconfirmed. No new tick or broad real-world pass.

Feature-by-feature evidence and remaining checks. Historical checkmarks retain their original build and scope; no new tick or Available upgrade.

Does it work today? Windows PC to your Android phone

Yes. Playing your own films from your Windows PC to your Android phone works today, in the test app. It is a test download, not on Google Play yet.

Based on tests up to Oct 28, 2026, 10:24 AM Eastern. Most of these tries used one phone (a Galaxy S24) and one second-household Windows PC (Windows 0.1.104, Android test builds tester57 and then tester58 from about 3:06 PM Eastern), with Nick present. Some used other phones. Nothing here is a promise that it can never fail. Tests after about 4:07 PM Eastern used the 4-core PC alone with Nick away and are marked as the 4-core AI tester alone on their rows. Overnight on Oct 28 the 4-core PC was updated to Windows 0.1.105 (and then to Windows 0.1.106, published at 1:26 AM Eastern, with most of its desktop fixes retested), and a Pixel 3 and a Galaxy S9+ ran unpublished test builds tester59 to tester61 with an AI tester, silent. In the second overnight update (through about 4:28 AM Eastern) the 4-core PC was updated again, to Windows 0.1.107 (published at 3:07 AM Eastern), and the Story Studio preview and Users watch-time fixes were retested; the Pixel 3 and Galaxy S9+ moved to the unpublished test build tester62, silent.

What real people have already tried

  • Away from home, on 5G through Beebo Relay: a 6-minute run played 5 minutes 45 seconds with 0 stalls and 0 disconnects (Oct 27).
  • Wi-Fi switched off and on during a real film: it resumed at the same place 8 of 8 times (Oct 27).
  • On the same Wi-Fi as the PC: 5 of 5 launches connected directly (Oct 27).
  • Seek bar, pause, 5 and 15 second skips and picture-in-picture worked instantly on 5G (Oct 27, Nick).
  • Changing the quality to converted 480p during a film played from the same spot after about 3 seconds, with no real pause (Oct 27, Nick).
  • Subtitles on the phone passed, confirmed by an AI tester and by Nick (Oct 27). Not tested on a TV, other formats or a second language.
  • Casting a film to a Samsung TV: after the film ended, pressing the seek bar played it from that spot and Replay restarted it from the beginning (Oct 27, tester58; Nick watched the TV and heard the sound). The first cast right after the TV was switched on did nothing.
  • Surprise me on the phone, from the PC on the same Wi-Fi: a random film started with picture and sound in about 1.6 seconds, changing to the next or previous film took about 3 seconds or less, and seeking to a new spot in a 1 hour 42 minute film took 1.2 to 1.6 seconds (Oct 27, tester58; Nick heard the sound).
  • In Chrome on a PC, the web player played, paused, sought, switched quality, showed captions that matched the picture and went into a floating picture-in-picture window that Nick moved and resized (Oct 27, Windows 0.1.104). Sound was not heard on that PC.
  • Windows updated itself from 0.1.104 to 0.1.105 in the app in 3 minutes 35 seconds and the start-up warning box did not appear (Oct 28, the 4-core PC, an AI tester alone).
  • In Chrome on Windows 0.1.105 the “Resume from…?” box now holds the film paused until you choose, on 4 of 4 films (Oct 28, an AI tester alone).
  • Windows updated itself from 0.1.106 to 0.1.107 in the app in 3 minutes 34 seconds and the start-up warning box did not appear; a copy of the downloaded installer matched the website feed’s hash (Oct 28, the 4-core PC, an AI tester alone).
  • In the Windows 0.1.107 app the Story Studio 10-second preview now shows a painted picture and plays from 0:00 to 0:10 (basic path only; Oct 28, an AI tester alone).
  • Users > View stats now shows plausible watch time on Windows 0.1.107: the week read 106 h 2 m before the update and 4 h 33 m after (Oct 28, an AI tester alone).

What is still open

  • The first play over 5G after a phone app update once took about 70 seconds (about 2 seconds earlier the same morning). It is being re-tested and is not called a bug yet.
  • Leaving Wi-Fi shows 1.5 to 4.5 seconds of black or frozen picture.
  • On the same Wi-Fi, 5 of the PC’s last 30 logged connections went through Relay instead of directly. A fix is under review and not merged.
  • In Chrome on a phone, switching from Wi-Fi to 5G during play failed in 3 of 4 runs on Oct 26. The phone app passed on Oct 27; Chrome has not been retested.
  • Home “Continue watching” was sometimes empty after a short resumed session. A retest on a clean account is still to do.
  • Casting to a TV: captions are still not seen on the TV (a fix is merged and was tried once on tester58 with the TV watched through a phone camera: the film did not reload when captions were switched, but no caption text was seen), and the first cast right after the TV was switched on did nothing and showed no error. The seek bar after a film ends now works (Nick, tester58).
  • Not tested yet: sessions much longer than 5 minutes, and two people on Beebo Relay at once.
  • On the phone app, closing Picture-in-Picture left the app sideways when auto-rotate was on (3 of 3 on a test build). A fix works on an unpublished test build only, so it is still open.
  • Opening Story Studio in the installed Windows app writes 38 error lines about painted character files and both character rigs missing from the installed package; the preview still draws.
  • The Campsite host card counting the host’s own game room as a guest is right on the unpublished test build tester62, so it stays open until a published build carries it.

Our scoreboard rates Playing films at 90%, Away from home at 90% and TV casting (Chromecast) at 90%, because items like the ones above are still open. A feature reaches 100% only when Nick and a tester both confirm it with nothing open.

Test app for sideloading: the scoreboard labels Playing films “Available (test download)” and Away from home “Beta”. Google Play: In development (not submitted).

Here is the short answer for each app: how many features are fully confirmed, how many are almost there, how many are earlier on, and what still stands in the way. The counts are worked out from the feature table further down this page, so they always match it.

What stops us calling it 100%

  • Known problems are still open. 29 known problems are open across 14 of the 21 Windows features. While a problem is open, that feature cannot go above 90%.
  • Fixes written or shipped, not yet tried by a person. For several features the fix exists in our code or in a recent download, but nobody has tried it on an installed app or on its real screen yet. Examples: Library sharing, Home layouts and the Picture frame screen changes (in Windows 0.1.105 since 12:01 AM on Oct 28).
  • Not yet tried on real hardware. Remote Desktop has never run on a real PC. A real restart of the PC has not been tried for Start with Windows. Phone speakers were mostly checked with the sound muted, so a person still has to judge the timing by ear.
  • Many features are still being built. 8 of the 21 Windows features are still labelled In development. Some, such as the Picture frame and Kitchen announcements, are switched off until you turn them on.
  • Needs more real-world use. Only 4 of the 21 Windows features have passed a real-world check (use like a real person, in real conditions), and 11 have passed a real-device check. So far the testing has been done by Nick and our own testers. A person is still needed on every release.

  • Google Play version 74%
  • Family achievements (opt-in milestones) 74%
  • Android TV and Fire TV screens 49%
  • Link a TV 49%
  • Photos and phone backups (timeline, albums, viewer) 49%
  • Phone Help (show your screen to another phone) 25%

What stops us calling it 100%

  • Known problems are still open. 29 known problems are open across 12 of the 31 Android features. While a problem is open, that feature cannot go above 90%.
  • Fixes written, not yet seen working on a phone. Several fixes exist in our code, but nobody has yet seen them work on a real phone or TV, or they are not in a published download. Examples: Campsite games, Chromecast captions, the phone’s Picture-in-Picture fix and the Trip Journal video export.
  • Needs more real-car tests. Beebo Auto has been tried in one real car, and one car is not enough to call it ready. Car party has no real passing test recorded yet.
  • Needs real TV tests. No approved Android TV or Fire TV has been tested yet, and Link a TV has not yet paired with a real TV. Casting to a TV still has open problems, such as captions not showing.
  • Needs equipment, or a person listening. Wake my PC needs a spare sleeping PC to test properly. Wireless speakers were tested with the sound muted, so a person still has to listen to judge clicks and timing.

What the numbers mean

The percentage on a feature counts the checks it has passed: built, automated tests, tried on a real device, tried in real use, and confirmed by a person. Any problem we know about and have not fixed keeps a feature at 90% at most, however many checks pass. A feature is called Ready (100%) only when a person has looked at it and confirmed it, not just because a test passed.

Both apps are still in testing. The Windows app can be downloaded today. The Android app is a test download that you install yourself; it is not on Google Play yet. Nothing here is a promise that a feature can never fail.

Testing transparency

Evidence, not assumptions.

Beebo uses local checks, AI-assisted hand testing and human reports to find problems. They are useful together—but no one kind of testing proves every device, route or feature.

Every published result needs a build, a scope and an honest limit. A human tester is still needed on every release.

Real-device checks recorded Oct 26, 2026, 9:20 AM Eastern

October 25 to 26: two households, real TVs and a Chromecast, 5G through Beebo Relay, and the new test build on two phones. What passed, what failed.

Two kinds of check are listed here. With Nick in the room at a second household, an AI helper drove a Galaxy S24 while Nick watched and listened to the TVs; the PC there is an old 2014-era 4-core machine running the published Beebo 0.1.102. On the home test bench, AI helpers ran a Pixel 3 and a Galaxy S9+ on the new unpublished test build (tester50) against an isolated test server (the Windows server code, not the installed Windows app), with the phones muted. The times are when each result was posted to the team’s test board (Eastern); the run times in the reports are given as written. We record the in-the-room checks as AI-driven device tests with a human observer, not as Nick’s own tests, so no Real-world check and no Ready was added, no percentage went up, and new open issues were added to six rows. A test that was not run is unknown, not broken. Casting captions, network switching during play, and several phone screens failed and are listed as failures.

Numbers come from our own test list (last updated Oct 28, 2026, 10:29 AM Eastern) and were worked out on Oct 28, 2026, 10:29 AM Eastern. They show how much of our checklist has passed, not whether the app is bug-free. A high code number means the code is built and its automated tests pass. It does not mean nothing is left to build: the open code items are listed under each bar.

Code built and tests passing is the share of the Built and Automated tests checks that passed. The separate Device and real-world checks recorded figure is the share of Real device, Real-world check and Ready to call Available that passed. It includes AI tests on real devices; it does not mean a person checked every feature. The final Ready check needs a human look, recorded by Nick. These separate figures keep their existing checklist method. Group figures are the average of their features and are never rounded up to 100. A feature shows "Code 100%" only when both of those code checks passed and no CODE item is still open; it counts as "Confirmed working on real devices" only when all five checks passed. Remaining counts are open road-to-100 items. All 70 features are counted, including those that are planned or on hold.

How to read this page

Four kinds of evidence. No shortcuts.

We separate what a check actually established from what is still unknown. A completed step is not automatically a passed feature, and a local result is not the same as a real-device result.

✓

Real-device confirmed

A named build was tried on a stated device, connection and feature path. It confirms that specific situation—not every setup.

⌁

Built or locally checked

Code-level and local checks help catch regressions. A person still needs to verify the experience in the packaged app.

?

Verification pending

There is not enough reviewed evidence to call this a pass or a failure yet. It stays visible instead of becoming an optimistic claim.

×

Needs more people or hardware

Some paths require another person, another device, a receiver, a tuner or payment access. One session cannot validate them alone.

Progress by feature · last updated Oct 28, 2026, 10:29 AM Eastern

Every feature: how far along, and what gets it to 100%.

How the percentage works. percentComplete is worked out from features[].checks and features[].openIssues by site-data/progress-score.js: Built 24, Automated tests 25, Real device 25, Real-world check 25, Ready to call Available 1 (only Nick records it). The first four add up to 99. A feature reaches 99 only when all four are true and openIssues is 0 (omitted means 0). An open known error caps the score at 90. An optional percentCap, explained by scoreNote, is a further limit. Check with: node site-data/check-progress-score.js. Realistic AI checks on real devices may count toward Real-world when the evidence covers actual use. Muted or state-only checks cannot prove behavior they did not judge. Only Nick records Ready. Each row lists its limits; all listed checks passing does not mean a feature can never fail.

Updated 19 of 70 features changed since the previous update (Oct 28, 2026, 7:26 AM Eastern). Highlighted rows (only those changed in this latest update) show the old and new percentage (the small mark on the bar is the old position), what changed in one sentence, and the date and time in Eastern. Older changes stay in each row’s notes as “Earlier update” notes. This temporary marker is shown while testing is under way.

How to read the “Left to reach 100%” column

100% means all five checks passed for the whole feature. Each row has a one-line summary and an expandable box, “What 100% means and what is left”, with what is already done and what is still to do. The remaining work comes in four kinds:

  • 🛠️ Build or fix (we can do this): code or tests that a developer or AI helper can write.
  • 📱 Test on a real device: needs a real phone, PC, TV or car; a computer test cannot replace it.
  • 🧑 Needs Nick: his decision, an account, money or a legal question.
  • 🚧 Blocked: waiting on something else, such as a careful security review or a decision.

Remaining items across all 70 features: 81 to build or fix, 112 real-device tests, 22 for Nick, 26 blocked.

What the tiers mean

Green is reserved for 90–98%. At 90%, the listed runnable checks may have passed while an open issue caps the score at 90%; an explicit record limit can also hold it below 99. Teal 80–89% means nearly there. The percentage still follows the recorded checks, never a colour choice.

99% and 100% keep their existing meanings. An open issue always caps the score at 90%. Colour never replaces words.

    Oct 24, 2026, 9:15 PM EasternReal-world checks on Oct 24: a second household through Beebo Relay, Chromecast on the TV, browser captions, and honest failures

    What was tested: Real devices, Oct 24, 2026 (afternoon and evening, Eastern). A Galaxy S24 on 5G mobile data to the owner’s home server (direct about 1:30 PM, Beebo Relay about 3:40 PM) and to a second household’s old 4-core Windows PC running Windows 0.1.102 (about 7:50 to 8:05 PM). The S24 and the Living Room TV on unpublished Android test builds (controls fix about 1:00 to 2:40 PM; a streamed film on test build 42 about 8:20 PM). The browser player on the S24 over 5G through Beebo Relay (about 8:25 PM), Chrome on a PC, a Galaxy S9+ and the S24 for Campsite, and two phones for Watch Together.

    What happened: Passed within the scope stated: direct and Beebo Relay playback from a phone on 5G; a real second household’s PC through Beebo Relay playing the original file (about 2 seconds to connect); the cast controls working by finger on the real TV and a streamed film cast with picture and sound on test build 42; three subtitle cues drawing in the browser player; a no-app Campsite guest joining from a phone browser; Chrome playback, pause, arrow keys and quality changes. FAILED or not working: a converted 720p quality failed twice on the second household’s old PC; casting a downloaded copy did not play on the TV; Watch Together did not connect for phones signed in only to the home server (test build 41 now says so honestly); Trip Journal “Save as a video” stayed at 0% on a Galaxy S9+; and the web player had keyboard-focus, show-page, blank Suggestions and owner-only-control failures (fixes written, not merged). Not tested: Wi-Fi to mobile-data hand-over, sessions over a few minutes, the phone pass-through cast route, seeking by dragging and captions on the TV, the Android app’s own captions, a guest game round or guest video in Campsite, the Android photo map on a phone, a second person on Relay. No percentage, checkmark or status label changed.

    Oct 22, 2026 (Eastern)Android 1.51-tester34 on four phones and Windows 0.1.98 on a PC: no crash logged, failures written down, one tick withdrawn, no tick added

    What was tested: The Android 1.51-tester34 (build 84) on a Google Pixel 3 (2:59 to 3:28 AM Eastern, and again about 4:00 to 4:26 AM), a Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra (3:00 to 3:16 AM, stopped early because the phone was in use; again 3:58 to 4:28 AM), a Samsung Galaxy S25 (3:54 to 4:29 AM) and a Samsung Galaxy S9+ on a child test profile (3:57 to 4:26 AM), then a Pixel 3 on a Windows 0.1.99 test PC (4:35 to 5:22 AM), a two-phone Watch Together, Campsite and Chromecast run (4:34 to 4:52 AM), a Photos run on two phones (about 5:25 to 5:40 AM) and a browser run on a second test home (5:08 to 5:12 AM). On Oct 21 Windows 0.1.98 was tried by hand on a Windows PC (8:11 to 8:29 AM and 10:45 to 11:00 AM) and a Pixel 3 ran tester33 (8:11 to 9:20 AM). All phones were muted, so nobody heard sound on a phone.

    What happened: No crash appeared in any phone crash log. Passed: the five tabs, playback and quality choices, Watch Together on two phones, Campsite join and a finished Tic-Tac-Toe game, cast controls to a real Chromecast TV (picture and sound on the TV not confirmed), music, audiobook resume after a force-stop, genre names in French, German and Spanish, photos for a normal member, and on Windows the picture frame (10 of 11 checks) and the five library folder types. Failed: no way to choose embedded subtitles or sidecar subtitle files, and no version picker, on the phone; Next on a downloaded episode online skipped a saved episode (results disagree between runs); text cut off at 150% text size; the guest page did not say the host had stopped; photo pictures did not load for a child profile; a Movie Night page showed a raw error; a browser could not open a film through the away address; the folders' own posters and NFO files were not used on Windows 0.1.98. App repairs are in unpublished test builds; server repairs are reported deployed. RETEST-1 has mixed results, with child delete-screen and sidecar failures and online Next/offline wording partial. Folder poster/NFO handling has no recorded repair. The Real-world check on Library, player and web player was withdrawn; no tick was added; Watch Together, Posters and info, Beebo Auto and Library, player and web player changed labels.

    Oct 13, 2026 (Eastern)Full device pass: two Samsung phones, a Windows PC and a real Chromecast; three failures found, several fixes written but not yet published

    What was tested: A full device pass on Oct 13, 2026, about 7:00 AM to 1:15 PM Eastern, by a helper driving the devices with the owner nearby: a Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, a Samsung Galaxy S9+ (Android 10), the Windows dev PC, a home computer running the published desktop 0.1.87, and a real Chromecast on the Living Room TV, on home Wi-Fi and on 5G mobile data. Builds: the published downloads are Windows 0.1.87 and Android 1.51-tester22 (build 72). The phones ran a test build of the current code made that morning (tester22 plus some unmerged fixes; the app still shows 1.51-tester22) and the PC ran the unpublished 0.1.88 test build, so none of this counts as a test of a published download. An earlier same-morning two-phone Campsite and phone-speakers test, and a Sea Battle game played by two people, are included in the rows.

    What happened: Passed on real devices: all five phone tabs on both phones; films (resume, play, pause, skip, quality menu, floating player on the S9+, 2x speed); a film on 5G through the direct route and through Beebo Relay (the relay first had to be switched on for the test account on the server, which the owner did); Watch Together on two phones (host, viewer, sync after a 45-second skip, leave and rejoin); a Car Party host and a passenger page on a second phone; Campsite hosting, a blank-name guest named "Guest 1", a guest reconnecting after 15 seconds offline, and 42 of 42 games opening (41 starting with a computer opponent; Crazy Eights played by hand); Chromecast with a person watching the TV (picture, sound, pause, play, skip both ways, a quality change and stop); radio and a podcast playing; a computer-made audiobook with chapters, jumps and speeds; sample music on both phones; playlists, watchlist, collections, Library health, Family Dashboard, Camp Jobs, a Packing List synced between two phones, Family Recipes; accessibility switches including Caregiver view; six languages on a phone and Spanish on the PC; the offline demo; the Share the app QR scan, download and install on the S9+; a trip link that opened on 5G with a photo and a clip once the away-from-home setting was on; all 27 Windows pages, five Home layouts, Customize layout, the update check and the signed-in browser player (17 of 17 pages, 720p/480p switching); phone speakers on two phones as a stereo pair. Failed: following a new podcast ("Your Beebo computer had a problem", three tries); the Trip Journal "Save as a video" (failed twice on the test build; with a fix on a branch it worked on the S24 for a 1-card and a 13-second trip, but the videos were not played back); the desktop Music window stayed silent at 0:00 (cause found and a fix written, not merged or re-tested in the real window); the ordinary trip link served from the home computer did not open from outside the home on 5G because the router did not let it in. Found, still open: the sound stops with the screen off by default (the Screen off: On option keeps it playing); the Music screen's Albums/Artists/Songs buttons overlap the "Mixes and radio" heading on both phones; a shared downloaded video was silent on a guest phone; the demo player has no subtitles button although its page says it does; phone volume buttons do not control the TV volume while casting; the live Car Party page still refuses a blank nickname (the automatic name is fixed in the code but not on the server); phone-speaker pages show a false Bluetooth warning and the PC speaker seat did not play in the surround test; no screen lets a customer switch Beebo Relay on for their own account. Not tested: Beebo Auto in a car, Android TV, Fire TV, TalkBack, a real wake of a sleeping PC, Live TV with a tuner, Chromecast to other TVs, converted films while casting, a first install from the QR on a phone that never had Beebo, accepting a library share, Walkie-talkie from anywhere, a real TV pairing code, Remote Desktop, Jellyfin, parental rules, an update installed over an older version, subtitles, and the new fixes on real devices. Ready to call Available was not ticked for any row, because the exact published downloads were not the ones tested.

    Oct 13, 2026 (Eastern)Campsite Sea Battle: two people completed a game over DIRECT-BeeboTV Wi-Fi

    What was tested: Nick hosted Campsite while a friend on a Samsung S20 created Sea Battle. Nick joined over DIRECT-BeeboTV Wi-Fi (BeeboDirect), the no-internet Wi-Fi Beebo creates for Campsite.

    What happened: They played a full game to the end; the friend won; Nick reported that it worked well and no problem was reported. This is the first recorded real-person result on the DIRECT-BeeboTV Wi-Fi route. Earlier Campsite tests used the same-Wi-Fi route.

    Scope and not tested: This is human testing for Sea Battle only; the other 40 Campsite games have scripted-guest coverage only. Nick's phone, both browsers, game length, and sound or graphics observations were not recorded. A phone hotspot and a guest on mobile data remain untested.

    Oct 12, 2026 (Eastern)Two-home real-device test: phone on 5G, home Wi-Fi and a friend’s Wi-Fi; relay, two viewers, library sharing, Windows hand test

    What was tested: A two-home test on Oct 12, 2026: a Windows PC at each of two separate homes on two different networks, one family server at a third home, a Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra on home Wi-Fi, on 5G mobile data and at a friend’s Wi-Fi, a Galaxy S9+, and a browser on the S24 and on a PC. Builds: the published Android 1.51-tester22 (build 72), Windows desktop 0.1.87 (published) and a 0.1.88 test build that is not published.

    What passed: Away-from-home playback (a direct connection to a home PC worked; a connection through Beebo Relay worked from a phone on 5G once switched on, with the first picture in about 3 seconds; the phone browser on 5G also played); play, pause, resume (a 63-second pause held its exact position), seek and quality switching to 480p in the phone browser and in the phone app; two viewers watching at once from one home PC, both connected directly in about a second; the phone app kept playing across Wi-Fi to 5G to Wi-Fi switches and through 24 seconds of airplane mode; sharing a library with another home (send an invite, accept, play, and “stop sharing” refusing new playback within about 30 seconds); the online games lobby loaded; uploading from the phone to the home PC (Space Saver backup: 3 files arrived); browse sort and filters, favourites and watchlist, playlists, radio, podcasts, Campsite game-room coverage using scripted guests (not a hand-played result for another game), dark theme, landscape and restart. On this website, 67 of 67 home-page links returned OK, and the installer and APK sizes matched the update feeds.

    Windows hand test: On the 0.1.88 test build (not published), about 35 screens were opened and looked right (Home, Movies, TV Shows, Trailers, Discover, Live TV, Audiobooks, Podcasts, Radio, Music, Photos, Upload, Switch to Beebo, the admin pages, Users, Watch History, Story Studio and all eight Settings pages). Not yet done: Log out on screen, the signed-in browser player, subtitles and keyboard-only use.

    What we found (fixed in the code): A shared-library guest could be dropped to a sign-in screen with no way back to their own home; a stopped share showed a wrong message and still looked active in the guest’s list; the web player froze for minutes after a phone switched from Wi-Fi to mobile data; the home PC could stop accepting viewers after many sessions because ports were not released; the app’s own picture-in-picture window did not close properly; some text was clipped at 150% text size; Library health showed a misleading counter and a stale “cannot be reached” line; skip-intro jumped over a 2:39 opening scene on one show; Auto quality chose 480p on a fast home connection; a share with downloads switched off still offered a download button.

    What we found (still open): A 40 to 70 second freeze after seeking far into a long converted film (a safeguard is written, but the cause is not fully confirmed); voices slightly out of sync after jumps on one TV episode (a likely cause was found and fixed in the code, but it is not confirmed on the real episode); the Read It To Me buttons were hidden behind the bottom bar (a fix is in progress); a new home name could not get its secure certificate until it was registered by hand; casting from a browser to a friend’s Chromecast was blocked because that TV is not yet registered for Beebo’s test receiver (casting to a TV through the phone app was proven earlier on the home TV).

    Not tested: Chromecast to the friend’s TV, Beebo Auto in a car, Watch Together with a second device, a real TV pairing code (Link a TV is switched off on the server; a wrong code was refused with a plain message), TalkBack, two people on Beebo Relay at once, the Windows Log out button on screen, a House-to-House share started from a PC, and the new fixes on real devices. The exact counted paths are in the progress table.

    What was tested: A two-home test on Oct 12, 2026: a Windows PC at each of two separate homes on two different networks, one family server at a third home, a Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra on home Wi-Fi, on 5G mobile data and at a friend’s Wi-Fi, a Galaxy S9+, and a browser on the S24 and on a PC. Builds: the published Android 1.51-tester22 (build 72), Windows desktop 0.1.87 (published) and a 0.1.88 test build that is not published.

    What happened: Passed on real devices: away-from-home playback (a direct connection to a home PC worked; a connection through Beebo Relay worked from a phone on 5G once switched on, with the first picture in about 3 seconds; the phone browser on 5G also played); play, pause, resume (a 63-second pause held its exact position), seek and quality switching to 480p in the phone browser and in the phone app; two viewers watching at once from one home PC, both connected directly in about a second; the phone app kept playing across Wi-Fi to 5G to Wi-Fi switches and through 24 seconds of airplane mode; sharing a library with another home (send an invite, accept, play, and “stop sharing” refusing new playback within about 30 seconds); the online games lobby loaded; uploading from the phone to the home PC (Space Saver backup: 3 files arrived); browse sort and filters, favourites and watchlist, playlists, radio, podcasts, Campsite game-room coverage using scripted guests (not a hand-played result for another game), dark theme, landscape and restart. On this website, 67 of 67 home-page links returned OK, and the installer and APK sizes matched the update feeds. Windows hand test on the 0.1.88 test build: about 35 screens were opened and looked right (Home, Movies, TV Shows, Trailers, Discover, Live TV, Audiobooks, Podcasts, Radio, Music, Photos, Upload, Switch to Beebo, the admin pages, Users, Watch History, Story Studio and all eight Settings pages). Not yet done: Log out on screen, the signed-in browser player, subtitles and keyboard-only use. Found, fix written and tested in the code, not yet in a published download: a shared-library guest could be dropped to a sign-in screen with no way back to their own home; a stopped share showed a wrong message and still looked active in the guest’s list; the web player froze for minutes after a phone switched from Wi-Fi to mobile data; the home PC could stop accepting viewers after many sessions because ports were not released; the app’s own picture-in-picture window did not close properly; some text was clipped at 150% text size; Library health showed a misleading counter and a stale “cannot be reached” line; skip-intro jumped over a 2:39 opening scene on one show; Auto quality chose 480p on a fast home connection; a share with downloads switched off still offered a download button. Found, still open: a 40 to 70 second freeze after seeking far into a long converted film (a safeguard is written, but the cause is not fully confirmed); voices slightly out of sync after jumps on one TV episode (a likely cause was found and fixed in the code, but it is not confirmed on the real episode); the Read It To Me buttons were hidden behind the bottom bar (a fix is in progress); a new home name could not get its secure certificate until it was registered by hand; casting from a browser to a friend’s Chromecast was blocked because that TV is not yet registered for Beebo’s test receiver (casting to a TV through the phone app was proven earlier on the home TV). Not tested: Chromecast to the friend’s TV, Beebo Auto in a car, Watch Together with a second device, a real TV pairing code (Link a TV is switched off on the server; a wrong code was refused with a plain message), TalkBack, two people on Beebo Relay at once, the Windows Log out button on screen, a House-to-House share started from a PC, and the new fixes on real devices.

    What this record establishes

    Specific paths on specific phones

    The S24 Ultra exercised development-build playback. The S9+ exercised the published test build offline and found problems. Neither session verifies every feature, Android device or connection route. The device sessions did not record counted checklist totals; automatic test counts are reported separately above.

    Known limits of a solo pass

    Not something one session can prove

    • Campsite guest joins and shared play need another participating device.
    • Casting needs a compatible receiver and a real network route.
    • Live TV needs the relevant tuner and broadcast setup.
    • Paid-service flows need authorised payment test access.

    Human testing remains essential

    Turn one result into useful evidence.

    01

    Use the invited build

    Record the app version, distribution and the device you used before you begin.

    02

    Try one clear path

    Note the feature, connection route and what you expected to happen.

    03

    Report what happened

    Successes and failures both help when the steps can be repeated.

    04

    Keep private data private

    Remove passwords, access codes, private media names and personal details before sharing.
